task.description: GH #517 / ISS-0184 is a holding issue covering 62 test-integration-svc failures across 31 files, NOT yet diagnosed to individual root causes. Observed error mix on a pristine database: 85x C22021 invalid byte sequence for encoding UTF8 (concentrated in ext02_webhook_dispatch_test and sch02_timer_polling_test, likely a binary secret or HMAC written into a text column), 19x C42883 operator does not exist text = uuid, 11x C42P01 relation does not exist, 11x C23514 check constraint violation, 11x C23505 duplicate key, 7x C23502 not-null violation. The issue's own acceptance criteria state: 'Each listed cluster is diagnosed to a named root cause and either fixed or split into its own issue' -- this is NOT a single fix, it is a diagnosis-and-triage pass. Your job: (1) run zig build test-integration-svc against a freshly migrated database and capture the current failure list (the issue's 86/62 counts may be stale -- re-measure); (2) cluster failures by root cause (the error-code groupings in the issue are a starting hypothesis, verify them); (3) for each cluster, determine if it's small/well-understood enough to fix in THIS run, or if it needs its own separate issue (per the acceptance criteria's explicit 'or split into its own issue' allowance) -- given 31 files and multiple distinct SQL error classes, expect MOST clusters to become their own filed issues rather than all being fixed in one BACKEND-DEV pass; (4) if any cluster is small, clearly diagnosed, and low-risk, you may recommend fixing it directly in this run's later steps -- but do not force everything into one run just because it started as one issue. This is expected to be a LONG-RUNNING diagnosis -- call `python3 tools/queue_heartbeat.py GH-517 r-co-2-loop` (then commit+push handoffs/global_queue.json) periodically, at least every 30-60 minutes, so this workspace's claim doesn't appear stale to other workspaces' gh_claim.py while you work (this is the exact scenario the new heartbeat mechanism, ISS-0615/GH-563, was built for).
acceptance_criteria: Current failure list re-measured against a freshly migrated database (do not trust the issue text's counts without verification)
Each failure clustered by root cause with the error-code hypothesis verified or corrected
Small/well-diagnosed/low-risk clusters identified as candidates for direct fix in this run
Larger/ambiguous/multi-cause clusters filed as their own new issues (ISS file + GitHub issue + global queue entry) per the acceptance criteria's explicit split allowance
Heartbeat sent at least every 30-60 minutes during this diagnosis via queue_heartbeat.py, committed and pushed each time

result.summary: Re-measured zig build test-integration-svc against a freshly migrated database (workspace r-co-2): 635 pass, 9 skip, 88 fail, 1 crashed, 733 total, 52 leaks -- the issue's stale 62/31-file baseline was superseded (surface shifted after 10 adjacent GH issues resolved 2026-08-07). The 85x C22021 hypothesis was a misdiagnosis: those are audit_chain_utf8_test.zig's expected, caught-and-handled internal errors proving migration 1107's guard works (all 4 of that file's tests pass). 93 real failures clustered into 11 groups, full detail in docs/issue-reports/ISS-0184-diagnosis.yaml: C1 (resource_id TEXT/::uuid cast mismatch, largest real cluster, ~18+ occurrences across 6+ files) -- collision found with already-OPEN ISS-0094/GH#348 (describes the same resource_id story from the opposite, now-resolved direction); updated ISS-0094.json + posted GH#348 comment + queued, NOT refiled. C2 (webhook_subscriptions.secret_ref never reaching freshly-provisioned tenant schemas) -- collision found with already-CLOSED ISS-0112/GH#375 whose fix (migration 1134) only covers tenants existing at migration-apply time; reopened GH#375 with reproduction + updated ISS-0112.json to REOPENED + queued, NOT refiled. C10 (env01_test 12 stale-row assertion failure) -- fully explained by already-OPEN-but-unqueued ISS-0100/GH#357 (leaked production-typed tenant fixture rows, confirmed live: 32 leaked rows found); added to queue, NOT refiled. C4 (5 ADP0x migration-column-check failures, verified live against DB) and C5 (repository_test content_hash, 10 blocks) already covered by OPEN/QUEUED ISS-0185 and ISS-0183 respectively -- no action needed. C3 (event_store store.zig:472 rowToEventRecord leaks 3 duped strings on duplicate-idempotency read-back path, same shape as already-resolved GH#526) is a small, well-understood, single-file DIRECT FIX CANDIDATE. C6 (svc04_admin_api_test, 6 blocks, HTTP validation status mismatches), C7 (exp601_tier_quota_test, 4 blocks, tier-profile override not applied), C8 (sch02_timer_polling_test, 2 blocks, scheduler skip-locked/rollback logic), C9 (idn02/idn03, 3 blocks, group-task-claim 403 + role-scoped list 500) are genuinely new, distinct, not-fully-root-caused clusters -- filed as ISS-0616/GH#565, ISS-0617/GH#566, ISS-0618/GH#567, ISS-0619/GH#568 respectively, each added to the global queue. C11 (2 OS-level socket errors, INVALID_HANDLE/CONNECTION_REFUSED under full-suite contention) noted but not filed -- likely non-deterministic infra flakiness of an already-repeatedly-fixed class (ISS-0182/0186/0187/GH-521/528/556); recommend filing only if it reproduces deterministically. Sent 3 heartbeats via queue_heartbeat.py (02:32, 02:46, 03:09), each committed to a separate main-branch commit and pushed immediately, per protocol. Updated ISS-0184.json itself to diagnosis_status TRIAGED with full cross-references to every sub-issue.
